**Isospin breaking in octet baryon mass splittings**

*December 20, 2012*

31 pp, 18 sections.

**Abstract.** Using an SU(3) ﬂavour symmetry breaking expansion in the quark mass, we determine the QCD component of the nucleon, Sigma and Xi mass splittings of the baryon octet due to up-down (and strange) quark mass diﬀerences in terms of the kaon mass splitting. Provided the average quark mass is kept constant, the expansion coeﬃcients in our procedure can be determined from computationally cheaper simulations with mass degen- erate sea quarks and partially quenched valence quarks. Both the linear and quadratic terms in the SU(3) ﬂavour symmetry breaking expansion are considered; it is found that the quadratic terms only change the result by a few percent, indicating that the expansion is highly convergent.

**Outline.** Front matter; 1 Introduction; 2 Octet Baryons; 3 Determining the expansion coefficients; 3.1 Partially quenched octet baryons; 3.2 Numerical results; 4 Octet pseudoscalar mesons; 4.1 PQ pseudoscalar meson flavour expansions; 4.2 Determination of the coefficients; 4.3 Pseudoscalar meson isospin splittings; 5 Physical values of the quark masses; 6 Comparison with `fan' plots; 7 Results and discussion; 7.1 Baryon octet mass splittings; 7.2 Physical values of the mass splittings; 7.3 Conclusions; A Systematic errors; B Tables
